title: Total probability
steps: A probability distribution must add to 1. The missing probability is \(1-0.4-0.2=0.4\).

title: Exponential growth
steps: A base greater than 1 gives an increasing exponential curve. It passes through \((0,1)\), stays positive and bends upwards. Only graph A has these features.

title: Domain of a square root
steps: A real square root requires a non-negative radicand: \(6-x^2\geq0\). Thus \(x^2\leq6\). Both endpoints are allowed because the square root of zero exists.

title: Reading a factored cubic
steps: Rewrite the expression as \(5x(x-2)(x-3)\). Its zeros are 0, 2 and 3, and its leading coefficient is positive. The curve therefore falls to the left and rises to the right, crossing at all three zeros.

title: Integrating a fractional power
steps: Write the integrand as \((x+5)^{-1/2}\). Increase the exponent by 1 and divide by the new exponent. There is no extra chain-rule factor because \(d(x+5)/dx=1\).

title: Reflecting a graph twice
steps: The transformation maps every point \((x,y)\) to \((-x,-y)\): a half-turn about the origin. The asymptotes become \(x=2\) and \(y=-1\), and the vertical intercept becomes \((0,-3)\).

title: Relative frequency
steps: The estimated probability left for the other nine faces is \((153-72)/153=81/153\). Divide this equally among the nine faces:
\[P(10)\approx\frac{81}{153\times9}=\frac1{17}.\]

title: Normal distribution and standard scores
steps: Since \(\mu=\sigma\), zero is one standard deviation below the mean: \(z=(0-\mu)/\sigma=-1\). About 68% lies within one standard deviation, so the area above \(-1\) is \(50\%+34\%=84\%\).

title: Estimating change from a derivative graph
steps: Between \(x=1\) and \(x=1.1\), the derivative is positive but falls below 2. Hence the increase in \(f\) is positive and less than \(2(0.1)=0.2\).
\[0<\int_1^{1.1}f\prime(x)\,dx<0.2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad6<f(1.1)<6.2.\]
The tangent estimate 6.2 is an upper estimate here; the decreasing slope puts the actual value just below it.

title: Stationary points of a composite function
steps: The chain rule gives \(\frac{d}{dx}f(e^x)=e^x f\prime(e^x)\). Because \(e^x>0\), a stationary point occurs precisely when \(f\prime(e^x)=0\).
Only the two stationary points of \(f\) with positive input can be reached by \(e^x\). Each positive input corresponds to one real value of \(x\).

title: Finding the vertex
steps: Complete the square: \(h=t^2-8t+12=(t-4)^2-4\). The square is smallest at \(t=4\), giving \(h=-4\).

title: Equal heights on a parabola
steps: Set \(h=12\): \(t^2-8t+12=12\), so \(t(t-8)=0\). Excluding the supplied solution \(t=0\) leaves the other intersection.

title: Equation of a tangent
steps: Use powers to differentiate: \(y=5x^3-2x^{-2}-9\), so \(y\prime=15x^2+4x^{-3}\). At \(x=1\), the tangent has gradient 19.
The point-gradient equation is \(y+6=19(x-1)\). Expanding gives the tangent.

title: Missing terms in a geometric sequence
steps: Three multiplications by the common ratio take 75 to 2025: \(75r^3=2025\). Thus \(r^3=27\) and \(r=3\).
The intermediate terms are \(p=75(3)\) and \(q=75(3^2)\).

title: Describing a scatterplot
steps: The points form a roughly straight, downward-sloping band. Larger television times tend to be paired with smaller exercise times.

title: Interpreting regression coefficients
steps: The slope −0.7 means that each additional minute of average daily television time is associated with 0.7 fewer predicted minutes of daily exercise.

The intercept 64.3 predicts 64.3 minutes of daily exercise for someone with zero average daily television time. These are predictions from an association, not evidence that television causes the change.
answer: Slope: −0.7 minutes per minute. Intercept: 64.3 minutes at zero television time.

title: Making a regression prediction
steps: Substitute the television time into the fitted line: \(\hat y=64.3-0.7(42)=34.9\).

title: Recognising extrapolation
steps: Two hours is 120 minutes, well beyond the observed range (about 0–60 minutes). The observed linear pattern need not continue that far. It would even give \(64.3-0.7(120)=-19.7\) minutes, which is impossible.
answer: The prediction extrapolates far beyond the data and gives an impossible negative duration.

title: Amplitude and period
steps: The amplitude sets \(k=2\). For a sine function the period is \(2\pi/a\), so \(2\pi/a=5\) gives \(a=2\pi/5\). Use radians.

title: Sketching a sine wave
steps: The second wave has amplitude 4 and period \(2\pi/(\pi/10)=20\) ms. On the requested interval it traces only the positive half-cycle.
Draw a smooth arch from \((0,0)\) through the maximum \((5,4)\) to \((10,0)\).
answer: A positive half-sine wave with peak \((5,4)\).

title: When two functions decrease together
steps: \(P_2\prime(t)=(2\pi/5)\cos(\pi t/10)\) is negative on \((5,10)\). Intersect the intervals; endpoints with zero gradient are excluded.

title: Classifying stationary points
steps: Write \(f(x)=x^2e^{-x}\). The product rule gives \(f\prime(x)=e^{-x}(2x-x^2)=xe^{-x}(2-x)\). Since the exponential is positive, the stationary inputs are 0 and 2.
The derivative signs are negative for \(x<0\), positive for \(0<x<2\), and negative for \(x>2\). This makes the first point a minimum and the second a maximum.

title: Completing the curve
steps: Join the left branch smoothly to the minimum at the origin. Rise to \((2,4/e^2)\), then fall towards the horizontal asymptote \(y=0\) from above. The curve touches, rather than crosses, the axis at the origin.
answer: A smooth curve through both stationary points, approaching \(y=0\) as \(x\to\infty\).

title: Building a loan recurrence
steps: Interest is applied before the repayment, so \(A_{n+1}=1.005A_n-5740\), with \(A_0=800000\).

title: Summing the repayments
steps: After \(n\) months, subtract the accumulated repayments from the accumulated original loan:
The geometric sum is \([(1.005)^n-1]/0.005\). Since \(5740/0.005=1148000\), collect the coefficients of \((1.005)^n\).

title: Solving for a repayment milestone
steps: The first whole month after this threshold is 154. The balances after months 153 and 154 are about $401,574.11 and $397,841.98 respectively.

title: Range of a composite function
steps: Composing gives \(g(f(x))=3/(x-1)+5\), with \(x\ne1\). The reciprocal term cannot equal zero, so the output cannot equal 5.
Every other output \(y\) is possible: choose \(x=1+3/(y-5)\).

title: Reversing a conditional probability
steps: Let \(W\) denote a win. The selection probabilities are \(1/6,2/6,3/6\). Weight each win probability by its selection probability:
The joint probability of selecting Amara and winning is \((1/6)(0.5)=5/60\). Divide it by the probability of winning: \(P(A\mid W)=(5/60)/(19/60)\).

title: Matching a lump sum with an annuity
steps: Use the monthly rate \(0.06/12=0.005\) and \(7(12)=84\) deposits. The lump sum grows to \(21000(1.005)^{84}\approx31927.7624\).
For end-of-month deposits of \(M\), the supplied table gives future value \(104.07393M\). Equating the two future values gives \(M=31927.7624/104.07393\approx306.7796\).

title: Mode of a continuous distribution
steps: The mode is the input where the density is highest. On \([1,e]\), \(f\prime(x)=-1/x^2<0\), so the density decreases from its left endpoint. Outside that interval it is zero.

title: Finding a percentile by integration
steps: The lower quartile leaves probability 0.25 to its left. Accumulate the density from the lower endpoint:
Exponentiating gives \(Q_1=e^{1/4}\approx1.284025\).

title: Proving a trigonometric identity
steps: Use a common denominator on the left. The numerator becomes a perfect square:
\[\frac{\sin^4\theta+\cos^4\theta+2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}=\frac{(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta)^2}{\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}.\]
Now use \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) and the reciprocal definitions. The identity holds wherever both sides are defined, so \(\sin\theta\cos\theta\ne0\).

title: Converting a tail count to a weight
steps: There are \(12600/21=600\) males. The upper-tail proportion is \(15/600=0.025\).
Using the 95% empirical rule, the upper 2.5% begins about two standard deviations above the mean. Thus \(x\approx76.2+2(6.8)=89.8\).
If using an inverse-normal calculator instead, \(z_{0.975}\approx1.960\) gives \(x\approx89.53\) kg. The empirical-rule estimate is the one used in the official marking guidelines.
answer: Approximately \(89.8\) kg using the empirical rule.

title: Comparing normal upper tails
steps: There are 12000 females, so 300 would again be 2.5%. But their mean is lower, making \(x-\mu\) larger, and their standard deviation is smaller. Both changes increase the standard score of this same cutoff.
The female upper-tail proportion is therefore smaller than the male upper-tail proportion. The expected count above the cutoff is less than 300.
answer: No; fewer than 300 females are expected above the cutoff.

title: A tangent shared by two curves
steps: The line has gradient 1. For the logarithmic curve, \(y\prime=e/x\), so tangency requires \(e/x=1\), hence \(x=e\). Its height is \(e\ln e=e\).
At that same point the quadratic has derivative \(2ae=1\), giving \(a=1/(2e)\). Substituting the point into the quadratic gives \(e=ae^2+c=e/2+c\).

title: Finding an antiderivative by differentiation
steps: Apply the product rule to \(x\cos x\), remembering the minus sign in front:
\[\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x-x\cos x)=\cos x-(\cos x-x\sin x)=x\sin x.\]
answer: The derivative is \(x\sin x\), as required.

title: Evaluating a signed integral
steps: Part (a) supplies the antiderivative. At the upper limit, \(\sin(2025\pi)=0\) and \(\cos(2025\pi)=-1\), because 2025 is odd.

title: Adding areas rather than signed integrals
steps: Area counts every lobe positively. There are 2025 lobes, so sum the supplied absolute areas:
This is much larger than the signed integral because the regions below the axis no longer cancel regions above it.

title: Expressing area in one variable
steps: The perimeter constraint is \(2\pi r+3x=100\), so \(r=(100-3x)/(2\pi)\). The triangle area is \(\tfrac12x^2\sin60^\circ=\sqrt3 x^2/4\).
Add the circle area \(\pi r^2=(100-3x)^2/(4\pi)\) and factor out \(1/4\).

title: Maximising a quadratic on an interval
steps: The allowable interval is \(0\leq x\leq100/3\), including the limiting all-circle and all-triangle cases. The coefficient of \(x^2\) is \((\sqrt3+9/\pi)/4>0\), so the quadratic opens upwards. Its maximum on this interval must occur at an endpoint.
The larger endpoint value is at \(x=0\), leaving all 100 cm for the circle.
answer: Maximum area \(2500/\pi\text{ cm}^2\), when all the wire forms the circle.

title: Two trapezoids
steps: Two equal strips over \([0,2]\) have width 1. The three heights are \(1,1/2,1/4\). Count the middle height twice:
\[T=\frac12\left(1+2\cdot\frac12+\frac14\right)=\frac98.\]

title: Exact exponential area
steps: Write \((1/2)^x=e^{-x\ln2}\). Its antiderivative is \(-2^{-x}/\ln2\).

title: Turning an area bound into an inequality
steps: The curve is strictly concave up, since \(y\prime\prime=(\ln2)^2 2^{-x}>0\). Each trapezoid lies above it, so \(3/(4\ln2)<9/8\).
As \(\ln2>0\), rearrange to obtain \(\ln2>2/3\), then \(\ln(2\sqrt2)=\tfrac32\ln2>1=\ln e\). The logarithm is increasing, so the ordering also holds for its arguments.

title: Area of a circular segment
steps: The smaller segment is the sector minus its isosceles triangle. In radians its area is \(\tfrac12(10)^2(\theta-\sin\theta)\).
It occupies a quarter of the circle: \(50(\theta-\sin\theta)=25\pi\). Divide by 50 and rearrange.

title: Estimating an angle graphically
steps: Add the line \(y=\theta\) to the supplied graph. Its intersection with \(y=\sin\theta+\pi/2\) is near \(\theta=2.3\) radians (numerically about 2.310).
Arc length is \(s=r\theta\), so \(s\approx10(2.3)=23\) metres. Use the curved boundary, not the straight fence length.

title: Using an angle of elevation
steps: In the vertical right triangle through \(Y\), \(\tan60^\circ=h/OY\). Since \(\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3\), rearrange for the horizontal distance.

title: Combining two triangles
steps: The 45° elevation at \(F\) gives \(OF=h\). On the ground, \(\angle OYF=45^\circ\): west and south-west differ by 45°. Apply the cosine rule:
\[h^2=\left(\frac h{\sqrt3}\right)^2+4^2-2\left(\frac h{\sqrt3}\right)4\cos45^\circ.\]
Simplifying gives \(h^2+2\sqrt6h-24=0\). Its positive root is \(h=\sqrt{30}-\sqrt6\approx3.027736\). Discard the negative root because height is positive.

title: Finding a bearing from components
steps: Use east and north as positive directions and place \(Y\) at \((0,0)\). Then \(F=(-2\sqrt2,-2\sqrt2)\) and \(O=(-h/\sqrt3,0)\).
From \(F\) to \(O\), the eastward component is \(2\sqrt2-h/\sqrt3\) and the northward component is \(2\sqrt2\). Both are positive, so the bearing is in the north-east quadrant.
\[\beta=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{2\sqrt2-h/\sqrt3}{2\sqrt2}\right)\approx20.905^\circ.\]
Use the unrounded height from part (b), and express the final bearing with three digits.

title: Translating a parabola
steps: A shift right by \(k\) replaces \(x\) with \(x-k\); a shift up by \(k\) adds \(k\). Thus the new curve is \(y=(x-k-1)(x-k-5)+k\).
Substitute \((6,11)\): \(11=(5-k)(1-k)+k=k^2-5k+5\). This gives \(k^2-5k-6=(k-6)(k+1)=0\). Only the positive solution satisfies the condition.

title: Counting solutions as a parameter changes
steps: Set \(u=px\). Because \(p>0\), the input interval becomes \(0\leq u\leq2\pi p\). The first three non-negative solutions of \(\cos u=1/2\) are \(\pi/3,5\pi/3,7\pi/3\).
Exactly two solutions means including the second but stopping before the third: \(5\pi/3\leq2\pi p<7\pi/3\). Divide by \(2\pi\).
The lower endpoint is included because it admits the second solution; the upper endpoint is excluded because it would admit a third.
